title: Unipotence of a point is preserved by every rational representation
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], meaning that every nonconstant polynomial in $K[T]$ has a root in $K$. Let $G$ be an affine $K$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix integers $m,d\geq1$ and homomorphisms of $K$-group schemes $i:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,K}$ and $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,K}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Suppose that $i$ is faithful: for every commutative $K$-algebra $R$, its map $G(R)\to\operatorname{GL}_m(R)$ is injective, where $G(R)$ is the set of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G$ over $K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every single point $g\in G(K)$, if $(i(g)-I_m)^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$, then $(r(g)-I_d)^M=0$ for some integer $M\geq1$. Here $I_n$ is the $n\times n$ identity matrix. No smoothness, connectedness or unipotence hypothesis on the whole group $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 9.19, printed p.171 (unipotence detected by one faithful representation holds in every representation); Theorem 9.18, printed p.170 (Jordan decomposition in algebraic groups), and Theorem 9.11, printed pp.168--169 (matrix decomposition). Specialization from perfect to algebraically closed fields.

proof.text: For every finite-dimensional rational representation $(V,r_V)$ of $G$, apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility] to $A_V=r_V(g)$, and set $\lambda_V=(A_V)_u$. These are invertible linear maps. If $f:V\to W$ is $G$-equivariant, its defining identity at $R=K$, $x=g$, is $fA_V=A_Wf$; hence the intertwiner clause gives $f\lambda_V=\lambda_Wf$. The tensor action at $g$ is $A_V\otimes A_W$, so the tensor clause gives $\lambda_{V\otimes W}=\lambda_V\otimes\lambda_W$. In the trivial representation $A_{\mathbf1}=I$. Its decomposition is $I=I\cdot I$: the identity is diagonalizable and $(I-I)^1=0$. Uniqueness gives $\lambda_{\mathbf1}=I$. This also treats the zero representation.

source.place: Theorem 9.18 proof, first sentence; Propositions 9.13 and 9.15; Theorem 9.11 uniqueness; representation conventions of Theorem 9.2.

proof.text: The preceding family satisfies every condition of [lem-sfb-tannaka-rational-point-reconstruction]. Thus there is a point $h\in G(K)$ such that $r_V(h)=(r_V(g))_u$ for every finite-dimensional rational representation. In particular, for the given representation on $K^m$ this says $i(h)=(i(g))_u$, and for the representation on $K^d$ it says $r(h)=(r(g))_u$.

source.place: Theorem 9.18 proof, application of Theorem 9.2 to the family of unipotent parts.

proof.text: By hypothesis $(i(g)-I_m)^N=0$. Therefore $i(g)=I_m\,i(g)=i(g)I_m$ is a decomposition with a diagonalizable first factor and a unipotent second factor. By the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility], $(i(g))_u=i(g)$. Step 2 now gives $i(h)=i(g)$. Apply the assumed injectivity of $i$ on points to the commutative $K$-algebra $R=K$: this yields $h=g$.

source.place: Section 9.19, printed p.171; Theorem 9.11 uniqueness; faithful detection expanded.

proof.text: Substitute $h=g$ in $r(h)=(r(g))_u$ from Step 2. The unipotent-factor clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility] supplies an integer $M\geq1$ with $((r(g))_u-I_d)^M=0$. Hence $(r(g)-I_d)^M=0$, as required. This uses no condition on other points of $G$.

source.place: Section 9.19, printed p.171, conclusion for all representations.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 9.18 proof and Section 9.19, printed pp.170--171; Theorem 9.2 and Propositions 9.13, 9.15.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-87ccd93c5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and both new nodes in full, checked them against Milne iAG2017 pp.164-171 (Thm 9.2 with conditions a/b/c, Thm 9.11, Props 9.13 and 9.15, Thm 9.18 proof, 9.19), and made no changes. The item's statement is unchanged. Its 4 steps follow Milne's proof of 9.18 and the remark 9.19. Step 1 builds the family lambda_V=(r_V(g))_u and checks naturality (equivariance at R=K, x=g), the tensor law and the unit law (uniqueness applied to I=I*I; the zero space is allowed). Step 2 applies Tannaka reconstruction at R=K to get h with i(h)=(i(g))_u and r(h)=(r(g))_u. Steps 3-4, correctly marked elementary: i(g) is unipotent, so i(g)_u=i(g); injectivity of i at R=K gives h=g; so r(g) is unipotent. The Jordan node is true over an algebraically closed field: it is 9.11, 9.13 and 9.15 with semisimple meaning diagonalizable; I tested V=0, dimension 1, unipotent A and the tensor of commuting unipotents. The Tannaka node is Milne 9.2 at R=K with lambda_V required to be invertible (harmless by 9.3); it allows nonreduced G and is unique because a faithful representation exists. Neither node restates the item, and neither has a proof or a cycle. My search of the DAG for tannak, jordan, unipotent, diagonaliz and reconstruct found no duplicate. Mathlib has only the additive Jordan-Chevalley decomposition and Tannaka duality for finite groups, so both nodes rightly stay unsplit. Both nodes are in the same unit, blueprint.from is inherited, same_as is [], there are no tool_uses and no SGA citation.
